input.summary: The alert is a true positive. The account behind it is jdoe (Jordan Doe, Payments Engineering), whose access has been compromised. Jordan is on PTO 2026-10-12..19 and normally uses macOS, but every jdoe action came from 198.51.100.23, an IP threat feeds list as malicious (bulletproof hosting, open Docker registry on port 5000, K8s API brute-force), using a Linux kubectl client. The same attack ran on all three payments-prod clusters: EKS 14:02–14:25, GKE 14:38–15:01 and AKS 15:11–15:34. Each time the attacker checked their permissions and listed namespaces, was denied on kube-system secrets and on creating a kube-system job, then read the payments-db-credentials secret. They created a privileged pod (debug-tools-7f9c) with host networking, host process access and the node's root filesystem mounted, then exec'd into it with nsenter to break out onto the node. The ArgoCD application-controller token was then used from that same external IP, which points to it being stolen from the node. With it the attacker created a ClusterRoleBinding, jdoe-break-glass, that gives jdoe cluster-admin. Using that access they installed persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet (kube-metrics-agent) and a CronJob (node-cert-rotate) that pull images from the attacker's registry at 198.51.100.23:5000, plus a NodePort service on port 30080. Finally they listed secrets across the whole cluster, which is what triggered the alert.
